definitions.explanation: not mixed with anything else; consisting of only one element
free from deceit or guile; sincere

examples.japanese: これは{純粋|じゅんすい}な{金|きん}だ。
{彼女|かのじょ}は{純粋|じゅんすい}な{心|こころ}の{持|も}ち{主|ぬし}だ。
{純粋|じゅんすい}に{楽|たの}しみたいだけだ。
examples.english: I just purely want to enjoy it.

examples.japanese: {子供|こども}の{純粋|じゅんすい}さに{心|こころ}を{打|う}たれた。
examples.english: I was moved by the children's innocence.

examples.japanese: {純粋|じゅんすい}{培養|ばいよう}した{細胞|さいぼう}を{使|つか}う。
examples.english: We use cells from pure culture.

examples.japanese: {純粋|じゅんすい}に{好奇心|こうきしん}から{聞|き}いているのだ。
examples.english: I'm asking purely out of curiosity.

notes:
COMMON FORMS:
- {純粋|じゅんすい}な - pure (attributive)
- {純粋|じゅんすい}に - purely (adverb)
- {純粋|じゅんすい}さ - purity (noun)

COLLOCATIONS:
- {純粋|じゅんすい}な{気持|きも}ち - pure feelings
- {純粋|じゅんすい}{培養|ばいよう} - pure culture (scientific)
- {純粋|じゅんすい}{数学|すうがく} - pure mathematics

CONTRAST:
{単純|たんじゅん} means "simple" while {純粋|じゅんすい} means "pure" - they share {純|じゅん} but have different meanings.
